page: Amazon Web Services r8i.metal-48xl is a memory-optimized bare-metal server powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 480 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8i.metal-48xl demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core tests, Passmark CPU scores, and Geekbench multi-core workloads. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read and write bandwidth, with uncached large-block read speeds reaching 585.17 GB/sec and write speeds at 232.99 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests, though single-threaded compression and decompression remain strong.

The server does not include local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps. The bare-metal architecture offers high resource density and direct hardware access, providing qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale deployments by eliminating virtualization overhead. It excels in memory-bound and highly parallelized workloads, as evidenced by top-tier performance in Redis SET operations and database operations. Additionally, the integrated AMX instructions enable top-tier prompt processing speeds for large language models, making this instance highly suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise database operations, heavy multi-threaded compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
